page: Amazon Web Services m5ad.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7571 processor. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and utilizes the x86_64 architecture.

A key differentiator of the m5ad family is the inclusion of bundled local storage. The m5ad.2xlarge includes a 300 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume, offering low-latency scratch space. Networking capabilities include a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included with this instance.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the AMD EPYC 7571 processor delivers modest compute capabilities. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng and Geekbench place the instance in the bottom 10% to 25% tiers. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks fall into the weak category, though Passmark memory and CPU encryption tests achieve average ratings. Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput are also on the lower end, reflecting its position as an older-generation general-purpose option.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m5ad.2xlarge offers a balanced resource profile with the added value of high-speed local NVMe storage, making it a viable option for workloads that require temporary storage without the added cost of EBS volumes. It is best suited for general-purpose workloads, development environments, light database caching, and basic web serving where extreme CPU throughput is not a primary requirement.
